data.note: This CME visible to the SW in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2 imagery. The source of this CME is a filament eruption best seen in STEREO A EUVI 304 to the SW with associated brightening and in STEREO A EUVI 195 starting around 2026-05-31T11:15Z. Additional moving/opening field lines and views of the filament are seen in SDO/AIA and GOES SUVI wavelengths beyond the SW limb starting around 11:46Z. Based on STEREO A EUV imagery, it is possible the source area of this filament eruption was near former AR 14443 (~S17W110 to W118) at the time of the eruption.

A small jet of filament ejecta is visible in SDO AIA and GOES SUVI 304 in association with this flare, and is heavily deflected to the North, likely due to this region sitting just North of a coronal hole.

data.note: Bright loop CME first seen to the East by SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2026-06-02T12:12Z, as well as by SOHO LASCO C3, STEREO A COR2 and GOES CCOR-1 in later frames. This CME has a faint, diffuse, preceding feature, but not a shock, seen ahead of the main bulk, likely due to the nature of the source eruption. The source of this event is a very gradual filament eruption seen centered at approx. S10E75 as seen in GOES SUVI, STEREO A EUVI and SDO AIA 304. This filament becomes unstable beginning at approx. 2026-06-02T10:30Z and gradually rises off the limb, but does not begin to disconnect from the disk until approx. 2026-06-02T12:00Z. This earlier rise likely accounts for the diffuse feature seen in coronagraphs before the main bulk of the filament ejecta. Field line opening, dimming and post eruptive arcades are also visible in association with this eruption in SDO AIA 171, 193, 211 and GOES SUVI 284.

The source of this event is an M3.3 class flare from Active Region 14455 (N13W05) which peaked at 2026-06-02T16:50Z as seen in SDO AIA 131. Opening field lines and dimming are also observed in association with this flare in SDO AIA 171, 193 and 211 with the dimming and opening facing Southward, likely indicating some Southern deflection.

data.note: CME first seen to the NE in SOHO LASCO C2 starting around 2026-06-02T19:48Z. It is also seen to the NE in SOHO LASCO C3 and GOES CCOR-1 but is covered by a real-time data gap in STEREO A COR2. There are two source candidates for this CME. The first and most likely is some faint field line movement from beyond the NE limb in SDO AIA 171 beginning around 2026-06-02T17:30Z following the filament eruption associated with CME: 2026-06-02T17:00Z. The second and less likely candidate is some additional minor ejecta from AR 14455 following CME: 2026-06-02T17:23Z, but measurement indicates that this second source candidate is not a good fit.

data.note: This CME is visible as a partial halo to the north/northwest in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1 imagery, and to the northeast in STEREO A COR2 imagery. The source is an M7.7 flare from Active Region 14455 (N14W13) starting around 2026-06-03T07:00Z as seen in SDO AIA 131/171/194/304, GOES SUVI 131/171/195/284/304 imagery, and STEREO A EUVI 195/304 imagery. A large ejecta is associated with this event which is deflected to the northwest. Additionally, an EUV wave is observed moving northwest of the eruption site, as seen in SDO AIA 171/193 and GOES SUVI 171/195/284 imagery.

cmeAnalyses.note: Approximate analysis of the fainter and wider partial halo front best seen in GOES CCOR-1 but also seen in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and not seen in STEREO A COR2 coronagraph.

Approximate analysis of the messy, two-lobed bulk front of this CME, based on the fit with three coronagraphs (STEREO A COR2, SOHO LASCO and GOES CCOR-1). There is clear northward deflection from the source location of the M-class flare (N14W13) but the associated erupting filament seems to originate a bit to the west from the flare location and is then seen deflecting northwardly, so the coronal signatures generally confirm this analysis. The half-width of the CME is based on later imagery in STEREO A COR2, as in coronagraphs there is/are later, wider, lobe(s) of this CME that seem to be integral part of it.
